correctness.rationale: Nondegenerate polar form B makes the off-origin quadratic-chirp autocorrelation Σ_x e_p(Q(h)+B(h,x)) vanish by nontrivial-character orthogonality, so its unitary Fourier transform is unimodular. Differentiate every off-origin correlation at θ=0: the coefficient is i e_p(Q(h))(e_p(−2Q(h))−1)Σ_xe_p(B(h,x))φ(x). Squaring, summing and using Parseval with Fourier normalization N⁻¹ yields D²E(0)[φ,φ]=8N²Σ_h sin²(2πQ(h)/p)|φ_hat(h)|²; with ||φ||²=NΣ|φ_hat|² the real Hessian eigenvalues are exactly 8N sin²(2πQ(h)/p). The kernel consists of Q(h)=0 labels, counted by the standard diagonal quadratic Gauss sum, including the discriminant sign for even rank. For an isotropic s, arbitrary phase f(B(s,x)) preserves each shifted correlation: in directions independent of s, cancellation occurs fiberwise; parallel shifts leave f unchanged. These p-phase tori contribute all Fourier tangent null modes, but no claim of their joint integrability. If Q anisotropic, positive Hessian on mean-zero real phases gives local isolation and the asserted smaller local stability constant; if isotropic, flat tori refute it. Independently evaluated 6 real Hessian quadratic-direction instances at p=3,5, plus split-form p=3,5 exact-flat cancellation; finite numerical checks corroborate but cannot prove all primes/ranks.
residual_risks: Assumes odd characteristic, nondegenerate homogeneous Q; global nonquadratic solutions not classified.
Hessian zero tangent directions from different isotropic lines need not combine into a smooth full-dimensional local solution manifold.
